I grew up in a house without a television. At the time I thought this was the cruellest thing my parents could have done. My friends talked about cartoons I had never seen, and I nodded along.

What I had instead was a library card and a lot of empty afternoons. I read everything: adventure novels, old encyclopaedias, the backs of cereal boxes. I didn't realise until much later how much those afternoons shaped me.
